lines.say: In 2015, Saudi roads killed thirty five people for every hundred thousand. Where is Israel?
Road deaths per hundred thousand people, since 2000. Lowest first.
In 2000, Britain is at seven. Israel, eight. The UAE, almost thirty.
Iran peaks at thirty three in 2010.
Saudi Arabia hits thirty five in 2015.
Then the Gulf turns it around. The UAE falls to five. Saudi Arabia, under fifteen.
Lebanon drops by more than two thirds.
Syria goes the other way. Thirty two in 2023.
Britain stays the champion, at two and a half. Germany, three point four.
And Israel halves its rate since 2000.
What makes roads safer, cameras or culture? Tell me in the comments.
Four. The best of the Middle East on this chart.

caption_en:
Two countries beat it. Neither is in the Middle East.

Road traffic deaths per 100,000 people, 2023 (WHO modelled estimates):
UK 2.5
Germany 3.4
Israel 4.0
UAE 5.1
Lebanon 6.9
Egypt 7.9
Turkey 8.1
Jordan 13.7
Saudi Arabia 14.7
Iran 19.4
Syria 31.7

2000: UK 6.9, Israel 8.0, UAE 29.5. Iran peaked at 33.3 (2010), Saudi Arabia at 35.2 (2015). Lebanon fell from 23.4 to 6.9. Israel halved its rate from 8.0 to 4.0.
These are WHO modelled estimates and can differ from national police counts.

Source: WHO Global Health Observatory, RS_198, estimated road traffic death rate per 100,000 population, 2000 to 2023. The animation interpolates between years.
Photos: Riyadh (B.alotaby, CC BY-SA 4.0), Dubai airport (Chris Olszewski, CC BY-SA 4.0), Beirut (Wusel007, CC BY-SA 3.0), Ayalon Highway (Ilya Platonov, public domain), via Wikimedia Commons.

caption_he: הרוגים בתאונות דרכים ל 100,000 תושבים, 2023 (הערכות ארגון הבריאות העולמי): בריטניה 2.5, גרמניה 3.4, ישראל 4.0, הטובה במזרח התיכון בטבלה. סוריה 31.7, איראן 19.4, סעודיה 14.7.
